name: Louis XI of France
summary: Louis XI strengthened royal fiscal and military authority while reducing the independence of powerful princes. He promoted selected industries through public finance, privileges and trade restrictions, retained hereditary distinctions, and alternated accommodation with the papacy and assertion of royal control over clergy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: His Angers charter grants noble status and inheritance privileges to officeholders and their descendants.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He reserves final decisions on taxation and royal finance to himself rather than representative approval.

capital-controls.rationale: He prohibits remitting French church funds to Rome to retain leverage and resources.

death-penalty.rationale: His government condemns Saint-Pol for treason and executes him immediately after judgment.

decide-locally.rationale: He curbs provincial princely independence and reserves central fiscal decisions to the Crown.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He commissions instruction specifically for his son Charles as future king.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: His own statutes establish the reigning king and his royal successors as sovereign heads of the order.

native-born-offices.rationale: He appoints Italian-born advisers to important royal posts.

no-business-privileges.rationale: His industrial program explicitly grants selected manufacturers exemptions from taxation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He directs public funding, equipment and skilled labor into silk production.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale turns on church property, privileges or separation, and the statement now asks only whether religious institutions should operate under the government's authority.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He imprisons powerful political adversaries and authorizes severe measures against rebellious nobles.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He combines customs barriers and import prohibitions with support for domestic manufacturing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He actively incorporates Burgundian and other princely territories into the royal domain.

notes: No inferred answers. All 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed against the record. Industry-specific support and naturalizations do not establish general technological acceleration, immigration reduction, or free-trade ideology. Hereditary monarchy does not by itself establish divine descent or a sovereign legally above all law. The Rosier des guerres was commissioned for Charles but is attributed to Pierre Choisnet, so its detailed propositions are not treated as Louis’s personal writing. Complete surviving letters and selected edicts were downloaded and searched; a full 1481–1482 correspondence-volume download timed out. Martial, fiscal and church policies are covered without treating nineteenth-century literary depictions as evidence. Inclusion failure is retained if necessary.
